references.desc:
The market-process theory of money's origin that
    Mises extends with the regression theorem; the founding
    text of Austrian economics.

The theory of production periods and the subsistence
    fund that underlies Mises's business cycle theory; also
    the source of his conception of private vs. social capital.

The natural rate / money rate distinction that Mises
    adopts and refines; Wicksell stated the problem but Mises
    develops the full cycle theory from it.

references.name:
Adam Smith —
    The Wealth of Nations
references.desc:
The classical defense of paper money as economy on gold
    ("dead stock"); the rejection of mercantilism; the framework
    for thinking about money's role in commerce.

references.name:
David Ricardo —
    Proposals for an Economical and Secure Currency
references.desc:
The intellectual blueprint for the gold-exchange
    standard later adopted in India and Austria-Hungary; the
    most systematic classical statement of the cost-savings
    argument for fiduciary media.

references.name:
David Hume —
    Political Discourses
references.desc:
The price-specie-flow mechanism; the classical
    refutation of mercantilism through the argument that money
    flows equilibrate automatically.

references.name:
Georg Friedrich Knapp —
    The State Theory of Money
references.desc:
The chartalist doctrine Mises spends Chapter 3 and
    Appendix A refuting; the most influential German defense of
    the view that money is whatever the state declares it to be.

references.name: Thomas Tooke & John Fullarton
references.desc:
The Banking School, whose reflux principle and
    real-bills doctrine Mises systematically demolishes in
    Chapters 15-19 as the intellectual foundation of modern
    inflationism.

references.name: Lord Overstone & Robert Torrens
references.desc:
The Currency School, whose positions on note issue and
    the business cycle Mises defends against their German
    detractors as the intellectually superior tradition in
    nineteenth-century banking debate.

references.name:
Friedrich von Wieser —
    Der natürliche Wert, essays on index numbers
references.desc:
The source of the phrase "Verkehrswert"
    (objective exchange value) and of the most sophisticated
    index-number method Mises critiques; an Austrian whom Mises
    treats with respect but disagrees with on key points.

references.name:
Irving Fisher —
    The Purchasing Power of Money
references.desc:
The contemporary whose quantity-equation approach
    Mises accepts in its essentials while rejecting its
    claim to have measured the value of money through index
    numbers.

references.name:
Gustav Cassel —
    Money and Foreign Exchange After 1914
references.desc:
The coiner of "purchasing power parity" and a
    contemporary ally in the attack on officialdom's
    interpretation of postwar European monetary chaos.

references.name:
Karl Helfferich —
    Das Geld
references.desc:
The chief opponent of marginalist monetary theory in
    Germany; the statesman-economist whose "circularity
    objection" Mises dissolves with the regression theorem.

references.name: Joseph Schumpeter
references.desc:
The theorist whose "catallactic claim theory" of money
    Mises engages with in Appendix A; a sometime ally whose
    methodological differences with Mises run deep.

references.name:
John Maynard Keynes —
    The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money
references.desc:
The principal antagonist of Mises's later career and
    the most influential reviver of the expansionist fallacy;
    only lightly discussed in 1912 but central to the 1952
    additions.

The representative of the social-contract origin theory
    of money that the regression theorem refutes; cited by name
    as the case Mises has in mind.

references.name:
Jean Bodin —
    Response to the Paradoxes of Monsieur Malestroit
references.desc:
The first systematic attempt to attribute price changes
    to monetary causes rather than to commodity causes, a
    founding document of quantity theory.

references.name: Franz Čuhel
references.desc:
The Austrian who showed that choosing among bundles
    does not imply cardinal utility measurement, refuting
    Böhm-Bawerk's last-ditch defense of measurement and
    clearing the way for Mises's ordinal framework.

references.name:
Michel Chevalier —
    Probable Depreciation of Gold
references.desc:
The contemporary of the California and Australia gold
    discoveries who predicted inflationary collapse from the
    gold standard — cited as a warning about premature
    monetary prophecy.
